items.title: Close the books in three business days
items.problem: Month-end close takes 7 business days. Accounts payable clerks spend about 3 of them matching bank lines to invoices by hand in spreadsheets, and the controller cannot see which close tasks are late until day 5.

drivers.statement: Cost: cut the 60 hours a month spent on manual bank reconciliation, freeing the AP team for supplier queries
Control: give the group controller ledger-locked numbers for the board pack by business day 4, as the audit committee asked in its 2026 findings

items.outcome: UK01 and then all EU entities close in 3 business days, clerks review only reconciliation exceptions, and the controller sees close progress daily.

items.title: Close duration falls from 7 to 3 business days
items.metric: Business days from period end to ledger lock, from the close calendar

items.title: Manual reconciliation effort falls from 60 to 10 hours a month
items.metric: Hours logged to the 'bank reconciliation' time code per month across AP

items.title: Bank lines reconcile to open invoices nightly
items.description: A scheduled automation matches the previous day's bank statement lines to open AP invoices, posts confident matches, and routes the rest to an exception report the AP team works each morning.
items.benefit_hypothesis: We believe matching bank lines to invoices automatically every night will cut manual reconciliation to exceptions only; we will know when reconciliation hours fall below 20 in the first pilot month.

items.title: Confirm the bank file format and match keys
items.i_want: a 3-day time-boxed spike that decides which bank file format (CAMT.053 or MT940) and which match keys (amount, reference, date window) the nightly job uses
items.so_that: the automation is built against the format the bank actually delivers

acceptance.given: sample files for the last 3 months from Barclays UK01
acceptance.then: a decision note of at most 1 page names the format, the match keys, and the expected auto-match rate on the 3 months of samples, and is linked on this issue

evidence: Decision note: CAMT.053, keys amount + end-to-end reference + 3-day value-date window, 87% auto-match on samples

items.title: Nightly job posts confident bank-to-invoice matches
items.i_want: the nightly job to post every bank line that matches exactly one open invoice on the keys decided in S-1
items.so_that: I only handle lines that need judgment

acceptance.given: yesterday's UK01 bank file has arrived by 01:00
acceptance.then: each line matching exactly one open invoice is posted with the bank reference in the journal memo (AC-3)

acceptance.given: a line matches two or more open invoices
acceptance.then: nothing is posted for that line and it appears in the exception report with every candidate invoice

acceptance.given: the bank file has not arrived by 02:00
acceptance.then: it posts nothing and emails the AP shared mailbox before 02:15

acceptance.given: a line matches exactly one open invoice except for an FX rounding difference of at most 0.05 GBP
acceptance.then: the line is posted and the difference is booked to the FX rounding account 7920 (AC-3)

items.title: Exception report is ready for the AP team by 07:00
items.i_want: a daily exception report listing every unmatched bank line with its candidate invoices
items.so_that: I can clear exceptions before the 10:00 cash position call

acceptance.then: the report is in the AP SharePoint folder with one row per unmatched line, its amount, value date, reference, and up to 3 candidate invoices (AC-4)
it still appears, with zero rows and the count of posted matches in the header

items.title: Day-by-day close calendar with named owners
items.description: A three-day close calendar replaces the current seven-day checklist: every close task has an owner, a due day (D+1 to D+3), and a dependency, and the team is trained on it before the pilot close.
items.benefit_hypothesis: We believe a three-day calendar with one owner per task will remove the idle waits between close tasks; we will know when the UK01 pilot closes in 4 business days or fewer.

items.title: Three-day close calendar is published for UK01
items.i_want: the close checklist rewritten as a D+1 to D+3 calendar with one owner and one due day per task
items.so_that: everyone knows what must be finished each day of the close

acceptance.when: the calendar is published in the close workbook
acceptance.then: every task has exactly one named owner, a due day between D+1 and D+3, and its predecessor tasks, and tasks that move earlier are listed for review (AC-1)

acceptance.when: the group controller and the Finance Ops lead review it
acceptance.then: each has signed the calendar's approval tab before 2027-02-12

items.title: UK01 close team is trained on the new calendar
items.i_want: a 45-minute walkthrough of the calendar and the exception report
items.so_that: I can run my tasks in the February pilot without asking for help

acceptance.given: the 8 people named as task owners in the calendar
acceptance.then: all 8 attended or watched the recording and the attendance list is attached here (AC-2)

items.title: Controller sees close progress every day
items.description: A dashboard shows, per entity and close day, which calendar tasks are done, late, or blocked.
items.benefit_hypothesis: We believe daily visibility of late tasks will let the controller intervene on day 1; we will know when no entity finishes more than 1 day after its calendar date.

items.title: Close progress dashboard by entity and day
items.i_want: a dashboard of close tasks by entity and close day with late tasks highlighted
items.so_that: I can intervene on day 1 instead of discovering slippage on day 5

acceptance.given: task status is updated in the close workbook
acceptance.then: it shows done, late, and blocked task counts for each entity and close day, at most 15 minutes after each refresh (AC-5)

items.title: Nightly job posts the same bank line twice when the file is re-sent
items.observed: On 2027-03-02 the bank re-sent the 1 March file at 03:10; the 04:00 retry posted 212 lines that were already posted at 02:00 (journal batches JB-8812 and JB-8820).
items.expected: Each bank line is posted at most once, whatever the number of deliveries (S-2.1).
steps: Deliver a bank file and let the 02:00 job post it
items.environment: UK01, production ERP, Barclays CAMT.053 feed

acceptance.given: a bank file whose lines were already posted
acceptance.when: the same file is delivered and the job runs again
acceptance.then: 0 new journal lines are posted and the run log lists each skipped line's bank reference (AC-3)

acceptance.given: a re-sent file that adds 3 new lines to an already posted file
acceptance.then: exactly the 3 new lines are posted

feedback.summary: Lines that match one invoice but differ by FX rounding of up to 0.05 GBP should still auto-post, or the exception report will be mostly noise.
feedback.resolution: S-2 gained S-2.4 (post FX rounding differences up to 0.05 GBP)

feedback.summary: Could the dashboard also forecast the close date?
feedback.resolution: Out of scope for M2; the calendar already fixes the target date. Revisit after two closes on the dashboard.
